# apple_app_store_review_detail (Resource)

Manages what App Review is told about a version: who to contact, how to sign in, and anything a reviewer needs to know.

A version has exactly one review detail. Apple creates one for some versions and not others, so this resource adopts an existing record when it finds one and creates it otherwise — either way, `terraform apply` ends with the configured values in place.

~> **This resource cannot be destroyed.** Apple publishes no `DELETE` for a review detail. `terraform destroy` drops it from state and warns; the contact information stays on the version.

~> `demo_account_password` is stored in Terraform state in plain text. Supply it from a secret store rather than writing it into the configuration, and prefer an account created for App Review alone.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "apple_apps" "example" {
  bundle_id = "com.example.app"
}

resource "apple_app_store_version" "v1" {
  app_id         = data.apple_apps.example.apps[0].id
  platform       = "IOS"
  version_string = "1.0"
}

# An app that works without signing in. Say so in the notes: a reviewer who
# cannot find the sign-in screen rejects the build.
resource "apple_app_store_review_detail" "v1" {
  app_store_version_id = apple_app_store_version.v1.id

  contact_first_name = "Ahmed"
  contact_last_name  = "Osman"
  contact_email      = "review@example.com"
  contact_phone      = "+20 109 255 8423"

  demo_account_required = false

  notes = <<-EOT
    No account and no sign-in are needed. Open the app and add a record by
    typing, by voice, or by photographing a receipt. The paywall is reached
    from Settings > Upgrade.
  EOT
}

# An app that does need one. demo_account_password is stored in Terraform state
# in plain text, so supply it from a secret store rather than writing it into
# the configuration, and use an account created for App Review alone.
resource "apple_app_store_review_detail" "with_demo_account" {
  app_store_version_id = apple_app_store_version.v1.id

  contact_first_name = "Ahmed"
  contact_last_name  = "Osman"
  contact_email      = "review@example.com"
  contact_phone      = "+20 109 255 8423"

  demo_account_required = true
  demo_account_name     = "appreview@example.com"
  demo_account_password = var.review_demo_password
}

variable "review_demo_password" {
  description = "Password for the App Review demo account. Stored in state in plain text."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  default     = null
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `app_store_version_id` (String) The ID of the `apple_app_store_version` this review information belongs to. Cannot be changed.

### Optional

- `contact_email` (String) Email address App Review should write to. This is where a rejection or a question about the build arrives.
- `contact_first_name` (String) First name of the person App Review should contact.
- `contact_last_name` (String) Last name of the person App Review should contact.
- `contact_phone` (String) Phone number App Review can reach that person on, including the country code — `+20 109 255 8423`.
- `demo_account_name` (String) Username of the account App Review should sign in with. Required when `demo_account_required` is true.
- `demo_account_password` (String, Sensitive) Password for the demo account. **Stored in Terraform state in plain text** — supply it from a secret store, and use an account created for App Review alone.
- `demo_account_required` (Boolean) Whether the app needs an account to be reviewed. Set it to `false` for an app that works without signing in, and say so in `notes` — a reviewer who cannot find the sign-in screen rejects the build.
- `notes` (String) Anything a reviewer needs to know: how to reach a feature behind a paywall, why a permission is asked for, what hardware a feature needs. At most 4000 characters.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique Apple-generated identifier for the review detail.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# The import ID is the App Store version ID, not the review detail ID: a version
# has exactly one, and Apple publishes no collection of them.
terraform import apple_app_store_review_detail.v1 8a41f2c7-93b6-4e5d-a1c8-2f7e6b4d0931
```
